title: Duality Gap In A Matrix Game
body_html:
Duality Gap In A Matrix Game

For a finite matrix game with bilinear payoff $g(x,y)=xAy$, define $$ L(y)=\max_{x'\in\Delta(I)} g(x',y), \qquad M(x)=\min_{y'\in\Delta(J)} g(x,y'). $$ The duality gap at $(x,y)$ is $$ W(x,y)=L(y)-M(x)\ge0. $$

The gap is zero exactly when $x$ and $y$ are optimal strategies. Indeed, $W(x,y)=0$ says that the best payoff player 1 can obtain against $y$ equals the worst payoff player 1 can secure with $x$, so the two one-sided guarantees meet at the value.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 2.7, proof of Prop. 2.7.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. L(y), M(x), and W(x,y)=L(y)-M(x) used for continuous fictitious play.
